title: Introduce OpenAI-compat tool hint encoder and fragment guard to stabilize tool selection across streams
author: Aditi Shah
release_notes: Adds OpenAI compatibility shim for deterministic tool selection during streaming and a structured-output normalizer; non-breaking, opt-in via config flag openai.compat.tool_hinting
description: Summary: This PR adds a lightweight 'tool hint' encoder to the OpenAI compatibility adapter and a 'fragment guard' layer that prevents mid-stream tool_choice flips when the model emits fragmented function/tool call messages; Motivation: We observed nondeterministic tool selection when large responses were streamed in fragments; downstream invocation systems would receive partial evidence and flip the chosen tool mid-stream causing duplicate tool invocations or aborted handoffs; Goal is to stabilize tool_choice semantics without changing the OpenAI-compatible API surface; Changes: 1) tool hint encoder: encodes deterministic, order-preserving per-tool hints into the stream as opaque, short provenance tokens (header: x-rw-tool-hint) that the invoke layer uses to lock the selected tool for the lifetime of a response; 2) fragment guard: coalesces contiguous tool-invoke fragments and defers decision until fragment boundary or signature-confidence threshold; 3) schema normalizer: aligns tool parameter schemas from external registries to the OpenAI function schema (type coercions, required->optional mapping, canonical name aliases); 4) tie-break policy: deterministic score+id tiebreak to avoid nondeterminism when scores are near-equal; 5) telemetry: new metrics rw.compat.tool_choice.locked_count and rw.compat.fragment_coalesce_rate; 6) opt-in config: openai.compat.tool_hinting (default false for now) and rollout plan; 7) docs and SDK: TS + Python compat tests and example; 8) e2e test harness that simulates fragmented streams and validates at-most-once tool handoff; Backwards compatibility: no API schema changes; behavior is gated by config and flag rollout for Dedicated/Private; Risk: subtle differences when models already rely on token-level heuristics; mitigation: gradual rollout and A/B canary; Why unique: instead of changing model scoring we add a streaming-level coordination primitive that is transparent to most callers; Technical notes: the tool hint tokens are HMAC'd short strings carrying (tool_id, seq, partial_hash) and are stripped before user-facing output; they are applied only in internal streaming frames; The fragment guard uses a small state machine per-stream to coalesce fragments up to 512 tokens or until an explicit end_of_function marker is observed; This avoids re-parsing partial JSON fragments mid-stream; See commit list and file changes below for implementation detail and tests.
commits: c1: add tool hint encoder and header plumbing; c2: implement fragment guard state machine and coalescer logic; c3: schema normalizer and alias table; c4: deterministic tie-break policy and unit tests; c5: add e2e harness and flaky test fixes; c6: docs + changelog; c7: bump compat flag default to false and add rollout notes.
files_changed: src/compat/openai/stream_hint_encoder.rs (new) -- short encoder with HMAC helper; src/compat/openai/fragment_guard.rs (new) -- guard state machine and coalescer; src/compat/openai/schema_normalizer.py -- alias mapping and coercion rules; src/serving/invoke/router.go -- honor x-rw-tool-hint header to lock selection; api/openai_compat.md -- docs for config and behavior; tests/e2e/openai_fragmented_stream.test.ts -- runtime e2e harness; docs/compat/rollout-plan.md -- canary plan and metrics dashboard; examples/compat/tool_hint_example.py -- usage example. Snippets: router.go: 'if hint := headers.Get("x-rw-tool-hint"); hint != "" { lockToolForRequest(reqID, decodeHint(hint)) }' fragment_guard.rs: 'if accumulated.len()>=512 || token=="<end_function>" { dispatch_coalesced(accumulated) }'.

Added KMS/HSM note to docs and redacted logging for hint tokens; hints are stored only in memory and never emitted to logs. See docs/compat/rollout-plan.md.' || Lena Gomez: 'Can we avoid the extra header and instead piggyback on existing invoke metadata? Headers are easier to miss in the proxy.' || Aditi Shah: 'We considered piggybacking; header chosen for minimal change to existing wire protocols and to keep hint opaque to model clients. Added comment in router to allow future switch to metadata field.' || Samir Kaur: 'Tests are comprehensive but there is a flaky case when coalescing large fragments; we should add a 2s fail-safe timer to avoid head-of-line blocking.' || Aditi Shah: 'Added timeout to fragment_guard and a unit test for timer expiry; reran flaky suite.' || Ivan Petrov: 'Approving pending docs and CI green.' || CI bot: 'All checks passed after rerun.'
